summary.title: Fenofibrate at a glance
points: A fibrate: mainly lowers triglycerides. One tablet a day, on top of diet, exercise and weight loss.
Three uses: severe hypertriglyceridaemia; mixed hyperlipidaemia when a statin isn't possible; added to a statin in high-risk mixed hyperlipidaemia.
Lipid ranges: triglycerides −40–55%, HDL +10–30%, given without comparator or time point.
Outcomes are modest: ACCORD-Lipid wasn't significant, and death from any cause hasn't been shown to fall.
Watch liver, muscles (more with a statin), kidneys, pancreas and gallbladder.

exercises.scenario: A GP wants to start Secalip Supra as the first treatment for a patient with ordinary high LDL.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC say?
options: Allowed, provided LDL is checked again after four weeks
Not an approved use; it isn't first-line for that
Fine, as long as diet continues alongside
questions.explanation: Fenofibrate can be first only in severe hypertriglyceridaemia, or when a statin isn't possible.

questions.prompt: When can fenofibrate be used alone for mixed hyperlipidaemia?
options: When a statin is contraindicated or not tolerated
Only once a statin and ezetimibe have both been tried and failed
questions.explanation: It stands in for the statin when the statin can't be used.

exercises.scenario: A partner's sales deck says 'fenofibrate reduces cardiovascular deaths'.

questions.prompt: How does the SmPC put it?
options: Clearly reduces cardiovascular and total deaths
Silent on outcomes; section 5.1 gives lipid changes only
May reduce coronary events; not shown to cut deaths
Shown to increase deaths in people with diabetes
questions.explanation: The lipid numbers look strong; the outcome picture is modest.

questions.prompt: ACCORD-Lipid showed 2.2% vs 2.4% events per year. Why isn't this a proven benefit?
options: It was stopped early for benefit
It had no placebo comparison arm
questions.explanation: About 8% lower in relative terms, but not significant.

summary.title: How it works
points: A prodrug: esterases convert it to fenofibric acid, the active form.
Fenofibric acid activates PPARα: more lipoprotein lipase, less apolipoprotein C-III, faster triglyceride clearance.
VLDL and LDL fall (fewer small dense particles); HDL rises.
Take with food; half-life about 20 hours; cleared by the kidneys, not removed by dialysis.
Micronised 160 mg replaces 200 mg capsules: milligrams alone don't tell you exposure.

exercises.scenario: A pharmacist is switching a patient from Secalip 200 mg capsules to Secalip Supra 160 mg.

questions.prompt: Does the dose need adjusting?
options: No: the micronised form is absorbed better
Yes: take two tablets to reach 200 mg
Yes: the tablet is weaker than the capsule
Only if kidney function is normal; otherwise stay on 200 mg
questions.explanation: Particle size changes how much is absorbed.

questions.prompt: Why does the label insist on taking it with a meal?
questions.explanation: The PIL says it doesn't work as well on an empty stomach.

exercises.scenario: A colleague asks why fenofibrate is easier to combine with simvastatin than gemfibrozil is.

questions.prompt: What's the pharmacokinetic reason?
options: Fenofibrate is removed by dialysis, unlike gemfibrozil
Fenofibrate carries no muscle risk with statins
Fenofibrate lowers simvastatin levels by blocking CYP3A4 in the gut
Fenofibrate isn't processed by CYP3A4 and doesn't block it
questions.explanation: That closes one interaction route, but the additive muscle risk remains.

questions.prompt: Which effect is only a marker, not proof of benefit?
options: Fewer heart attacks in FIELD's primary result
Fewer strokes in pooled fibrate trials
A fall in CRP and uric acid
questions.explanation: Changes in blood markers aren't outcomes.

summary.title: History
points: French molecule (Fournier), in use since 1975; Lipanthyl in the EU, Tricor in the US from 1998.
Many formulations: micronised, nanoparticle, prolonged-release; Secalip Supra authorised in Spain in 2000.
2009 Article 31 referral: fibrates kept, but not first-line, except statin intolerance and severe hypertriglyceridaemia.
Fenofibrate alone kept a statin add-on indication, based on ACCORD-Lipid; combinations Pravafenix (2011) and Cholib (2013) followed.
The US withdrew fenofibric acid's statin add-on approval in 2016, from the same evidence.

exercises.scenario: A US partner says: 'The FDA removed the statin add-on, so the EU indication must be gone too.'

questions.prompt: What's accurate?
options: The EU kept it; the US move was about fenofibric acid
The EU also withdrew it in 2016
The EU never had an add-on indication for fenofibrate
questions.explanation: Same trial data, different conclusions; Cholib remains authorised in the EU.

questions.prompt: What kind of procedure was the 2009 fibrate review?
questions.explanation: Triggered by the UK on 20 October 2009.

exercises.scenario: Why do Cholib and Pravafenix have EPARs but Secalip Supra doesn't?

questions.prompt: Choose the explanation.
options: Secalip Supra predates EPARs being written
EPARs are only written for generics and biosimilars
questions.explanation: EPARs come with central authorisation.

questions.prompt: What was the referral's main reason for moving fibrates to second-line?
options: Limited benefit evidence, not new harms
Manufacturing problems at Fournier's French sites
A rise in deaths in FIELD
questions.explanation: The benefit side of the balance shifted.

summary.title: What it's approved for
points: Every use is an adjunct to diet and non-drug measures; secondary causes are treated first.
Use 1: severe hypertriglyceridaemia — the one place it can be first-line. The EU sets no number.
Use 2: mixed hyperlipidaemia when a statin is contraindicated or not tolerated.
Use 3: high-risk mixed hyperlipidaemia on a statin, when triglycerides and HDL stay uncontrolled.
No outcome promise, no under-18s; recheck lipids and change course if the response is inadequate.

exercises.scenario: A man with type 2 diabetes, on simvastatin, LDL at goal, triglycerides and HDL still poor, high risk.

questions.prompt: Which indication fits?
options: Use 3: add-on to a statin in high-risk mixed hyperlipidaemia
None, because fenofibrate can't be combined with a statin in the EU
questions.explanation: High risk, on a statin, and triglycerides/HDL uncontrolled: all three conditions are met.

questions.prompt: His triglycerides are high because his diabetes is badly controlled. What first?
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled diabetes is a listed secondary cause.

exercises.scenario: Compare the EU and US labels.

questions.prompt: What does the US Tricor label lack?
questions.explanation: The US uses are severe hypertriglyceridaemia and LDL lowering when recommended LDL treatment isn't possible.

questions.prompt: A team member quotes '500 mg/dL' as the EU threshold for 'severe'. Is that right?
options: It's the ESC threshold for fibrates
It's the threshold used for children
No: it's the US label's number
questions.explanation: Roughly 5.6 mmol/L, shown only to mark the difference.

summary.title: Strengths and products
points: Secalip Supra: 160 mg micronised film-coated tablet; lactose and soy lecithin matter for patients. MAH Lacer.
Same product elsewhere: Lipanthyl (France), Lipidil-Ter (Germany), Supralip (UK).
Secalip 145 nanoparticle, Supra 160 micronised and 200 capsule are interchangeable at the same dose.
Labels copy each other: the 250 mg SmPC contains a sentence about other products.
Combinations: Cholib (simvastatin), Pravafenix (pravastatin), Spanish rosuvastatin + fenofibrate (substitution); none with ezetimibe.

exercises.scenario: A patient with a peanut allergy is prescribed Secalip Supra.

questions.prompt: What's the problem?
options: Only a problem if taken with food
It's contraindicated because of the soy
Fine if she takes an antihistamine
None; soy lecithin is safe even with a peanut allergy
questions.explanation: Section 4.3 lists peanut and soy allergy.

questions.prompt: She was on Secalip 145 mg before. Can she move to 160 mg without a dose change?
options: No: 160 mg is a higher dose than 145 mg
No: the 145 mg tablet is stronger
Only after a two-week washout to avoid double exposure
Yes: the three forms are interchangeable
questions.explanation: Particle size explains the different milligram numbers.

exercises.scenario: A BD lead asks which fenofibrate combinations exist and what they're for.

questions.prompt: Which is licensed only as substitution for separate tablets?
options: Cholib, the EU-wide fenofibrate and simvastatin tablet
questions.explanation: Cholib and Pravafenix require LDL controlled on the matching statin; the rosuvastatin products replace the same doses taken separately.

questions.prompt: Which partner is missing from every combination?
questions.explanation: No EU fenofibrate licence reviewed names ezetimibe.

summary.title: How it's taken
points: One tablet a day with a meal, swallowed whole. Diet and exercise continue.
eGFR below 30: contraindicated. 30–59: max 67 mg micronised, which a 160 mg tablet can't provide.
Creatinine in the first 3 months; interrupt if it rises over 50% above ULN.
Transaminases every 3 months in year one; stop above 3× ULN.
Not in liver impairment, under-18s or breastfeeding; pregnancy only after weighing benefit and risk.

exercises.scenario: A 70-year-old on Secalip Supra has an eGFR of 45.

questions.prompt: What does the label imply?
options: Fenofibrate is contraindicated at this level
This tablet exceeds the dose cap; use another product
Split the tablet and take half daily to stay under the cap
questions.explanation: This tablet can't meet its own label's limit at eGFR 30–59, and it can't be split.

questions.prompt: A year later his eGFR falls to 25 and stays there.
questions.explanation: Below 30 it must not be used, and dialysis doesn't remove fenofibrate.

exercises.scenario: A patient on fenofibrate has a creatinine rise at month 2.

questions.prompt: When must treatment be interrupted?
options: A rise of more than 50% above ULN
Any rise in creatinine at all
Never; the rise is always harmless
questions.explanation: Creatinine rises are common and usually stable, but the rule still applies.

questions.prompt: He forgot yesterday's dose.
options: Take it on an empty stomach to catch up faster
Skip the rest of the week
Take the next one with the next meal; no doubling
questions.explanation: The PIL's missed-dose rule.

summary.title: Reading a clinical trial
points: The primary endpoint decides success; everything else is supporting.
Give absolute and relative effects, with comparator and time; for lipid trials, each arm's change and the difference.
A CI including 1.0 means not significant; NNT only makes sense when the difference is real.
Drop-in (FIELD: 17% vs 8% started other lipid drugs) can hide an effect.
Subgroups need an interaction test; ACCORD's were p = 0.057 (lipids) and p = 0.01 (sex).

exercises.scenario: FIELD's primary result: HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.75–1.05).

questions.prompt: What does it tell you?
options: It proves an 11% reduction in events
It includes 1.0, so it's compatible with no effect
Between 75% and 105% of people benefited from the treatment
questions.explanation: p = 0.16; not significant.

questions.prompt: Should you quote an NNT for FIELD's primary result?
options: Yes: about 143 people treated for five years per event avoided
No: the primary result wasn't significant
Only for the women in the trial
questions.explanation: The NNT of about 71 applies to total cardiovascular events, a secondary outcome.

exercises.scenario: A slide claims fenofibrate 'works in people with high triglycerides and low HDL' based on ACCORD-Lipid.

questions.prompt: What's the right way to hold that claim?
options: As a question, not an answer
As disproven by the main result
questions.explanation: Subgroup findings raise questions; they don't settle them.

questions.prompt: Cholib study 0501 needed better triglycerides/HDL and non-inferior LDL. It missed LDL non-inferiority. What does that mean?
options: The combination was better on LDL as well as triglycerides
The trial failed on every endpoint
LDL wasn't measured in this study
Doubling the statin did more for LDL
questions.explanation: It met two goals and missed the third.

summary.title: The pivotal trials
points: FIELD (diabetes, no statin): primary result not significant; total CV events lower; drop-in may have hidden effect.
FIELD also showed more pancreatitis and pulmonary embolism, and less retinopathy laser treatment.
ACCORD-Lipid (on simvastatin): HR 0.92, not significant; subgroup with high TG / low HDL better, women possibly worse.
The EU kept fenofibrate and granted the statin add-on from ACCORD; the US went the other way in 2016.
LENS: slowed diabetic eye disease (HR 0.73), but it isn't an EU indication.

exercises.scenario: An ophthalmology partner wants to market Secalip Supra for diabetic retinopathy, citing LENS.

questions.prompt: What's the position?
options: Positive, but not an EU indication
LENS created a new EU indication for diabetic retinopathy
questions.explanation: Outside the label; it also showed no effect on sight or quality of life.

questions.prompt: What did LENS show about kidney function?
options: It caused kidney failure in some
questions.explanation: A familiar fenofibrate effect.

exercises.scenario: The regulator's decision rested on trials that both missed their primary endpoints.

questions.prompt: Which trial supported the add-on-to-a-statin indication?
options: FIELD, through its total cardiovascular events result
questions.explanation: Its subgroup data, printed in the label alongside the warning about women.

questions.prompt: Which two FIELD safety figures does the SmPC quote?
options: Stroke and death from any cause
questions.explanation: Both about 1.6 times as often as on placebo.

summary.title: Combination trials
points: Licences name: 'a statin' (Supra), simvastatin (Cholib), pravastatin or moderate statin (Pravafenix), rosuvastatin (Spain, substitution).
No EU fenofibrate licence names ezetimibe; the gallstone caution comes from the ezetimibe SmPC.
Statin + fibrate raises muscle risk: reserve for severe dyslipidaemia at high risk, no muscle history, strict monitoring.
Cholib studies: big triglyceride and HDL gains; LDL non-inferiority missed (0501).
Pravafenix enrolled people not at LDL goal, but is licensed for people at goal.

exercises.scenario: A partner wants to develop a fenofibrate + ezetimibe single tablet for the EU.

questions.prompt: What does the evidence and labelling picture look like?
options: Already licensed EU-wide, as part of the Cholib range
Only a 12-week lipid trial; no licence
questions.explanation: The Secalip Supra SmPC has no ezetimibe line at all.

questions.prompt: If gallstones are suspected on the combination, what does the ezetimibe SmPC say?
options: Continue and recheck in a year
Halve the ezetimibe dose and repeat the ultrasound later
questions.explanation: That caution sits in the ezetimibe label, not fenofibrate's.

exercises.scenario: Look at the Pravafenix pivotal study.

questions.prompt: What's the gap between the trial and the licence?
options: Trial: not at LDL goal; licence: at goal
questions.explanation: Worth reading about in the EPAR.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the three evidence columns (alone, + statin, + statin + ezetimibe) is right?
options: It shows what evidence exists, not what's best
They were compared head-to-head in a single factorial trial
questions.explanation: No trial compared all three.

summary.title: Heart-attack and stroke outcomes
points: SmPC: fibrates may reduce coronary events; not shown to reduce death from any cause.
FIELD: fewer non-fatal heart attacks, coronary deaths not reduced; ACCORD-Lipid: nothing significant.
No stroke benefit, in either trial or the pooled analysis.
2010 meta-analysis (18 trials): −10% major CV events, −13% coronary events; only 3 trials used fenofibrate.
PROMINENT (pemafibrate) was negative, but it's a different molecule.

exercises.scenario: A partner cites '13% fewer coronary events with fibrates' in a fenofibrate pitch.

questions.prompt: What's the most important caveat?
questions.explanation: Class-level and relative; absolute benefit depends on baseline risk.

questions.prompt: Someone says PROMINENT proves fenofibrate doesn't work.
options: PROMINENT was a head-to-head with FIELD
questions.explanation: Context for the class, nothing more.

exercises.scenario: Sort the evidence into 'supported', 'not shown' and 'open'.

questions.prompt: Which is 'not shown'?
options: Fewer total CV events in FIELD (secondary)
Fewer coronary events across pooled fibrate trials
questions.explanation: FIELD, ACCORD and the pooled analysis show no effect on death.

questions.prompt: How do the EU and US labels frame the same trials?
options: They contradict each other on the data
The US label is more positive
questions.explanation: Both accurate; different emphasis.

summary.title: Side effects
points: Common: digestive symptoms, raised transaminases, raised homocysteine.
Uncommon: headache, venous clots, pancreatitis, gallstones, rash, muscle problems, raised creatinine.
FIELD: pancreatitis 0.8% vs 0.5%, pulmonary embolism 1.1% vs 0.7% over 5 years.
Stop and seek help for muscle pain, abdominal pain, chest pain with breathlessness, leg swelling, jaundice.
Creatinine often rises, usually stable and reversible; interrupt above 50% over ULN.

exercises.scenario: A patient on fenofibrate develops sudden chest pain and breathlessness.

questions.prompt: Why is this urgent?
options: It shows triglycerides are falling fast
It can signal a pulmonary embolism
It means the dose is too low
It's the usual digestive side effect
questions.explanation: Stop and get medical help immediately.

questions.prompt: Another patient has severe upper abdominal pain.
options: Suspect pancreatitis: stop and seek help
questions.explanation: Pancreatitis was 1.6× as frequent as on placebo in FIELD.

exercises.scenario: The EU and US 'common side effects' lists differ.

questions.prompt: Why?
options: One of the two labels is wrong
The US uses only post-marketing data
questions.explanation: The lists don't contradict each other.

questions.prompt: What might explain the higher rate of vein clots, according to the SmPC?
questions.explanation: Homocysteine rose about 6.5 µmol/L in FIELD and fell back after stopping.

summary.title: Who shouldn't take it, and interactions
points: Never: liver impairment, gallbladder disease, eGFR below 30, pancreatitis (unless from high TG), fibrate/ketoprofen photosensitivity, peanut or soy allergy.
Muscle risk higher over 70, with muscle disorders, kidney impairment, hypothyroidism, heavy drinking.
Warfarin: cut the anticoagulant by about a third, adjust by INR.
Ciclosporin: kidney impairment; glitazones: paradoxical HDL fall; narrow-index CYP2C9 drugs: monitor.
Cholib is stricter: eGFR below 60, pregnancy, and simvastatin's rules too.

exercises.scenario: A patient on warfarin is starting fenofibrate.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC recommend?
options: No change is needed to warfarin
Double the fenofibrate dose instead of changing warfarin
Cut it by about a third, then adjust by INR
questions.explanation: Fenofibrate strengthens oral anticoagulants.

questions.prompt: She also had a light-sensitivity reaction to ketoprofen gel years ago.
options: Use with sunscreen and avoid summer sun exposure
questions.explanation: A previous photosensitivity reaction to a fibrate or ketoprofen rules it out.

exercises.scenario: A switch from separate tablets to Cholib is proposed for a patient with eGFR 50.

questions.prompt: Is it possible?
options: Yes: Cholib is less strict on kidneys
No: Cholib needs eGFR of 60 or more
Yes, at half the usual dose
questions.explanation: The combination inherits simvastatin's rules as well as fenofibrate's.

questions.prompt: Which further interaction does the SmPC flag for a diabetic patient?
questions.explanation: Fenofibrate's interaction list is limited to what the SmPC itself names.

summary.title: Pharmacovigilance
points: Fenofibrate's PSUSAs (data to 2017 and 2020) ended in maintenance: no label change.
The biggest review (2009–2011) changed its place because of limited benefit, not new harms.
Cholib's RMP: identified risks (gallstones, pancreatitis, muscle, liver, clots…) and potential risks (more CV events in women, homocysteine).
Missing information: under-18s, pregnancy, severe kidney impairment, liver insufficiency.
The 'women' signal travelled from an ACCORD subgroup into the SmPC and then the RMP.

exercises.scenario: Your team is preparing a safety briefing for a Cholib in-licensing.

questions.prompt: Which risk is 'potential' rather than 'identified' in Cholib's RMP?
questions.explanation: A possible link, not established, traced back to ACCORD-Lipid (interaction p = 0.01).

questions.prompt: What additional safety measures does the RMP require?
questions.explanation: All risks are handled through routine measures.

exercises.scenario: A colleague thinks benefit-risk changes only come from new side effects.

questions.prompt: What does fenofibrate's history show?
options: The referral found new liver toxicity
Only new side effects change the balance
Balance can shift on the benefit side
questions.explanation: Benefit-risk can move either way.

questions.prompt: What should trigger a refresh of this module?
options: A new generic launched in Spain
A PSUSA outcome other than maintenance
A change in the reimbursed price in any EU country
questions.explanation: Also a new SmPC revision, or a safety signal or DHPC.

summary.title: ESC guidelines
points: 2019: fibrate + statin 'may be considered' (IIb) when LDL is at goal and triglycerides stay above 2.3 mmol/L.
Icosapent ethyl ranks higher (IIa) for raised triglycerides on a statin.
2025: no new fibrate recommendation; fibrates described as having minimal impact on major CV events.
Statin intolerance: ezetimibe and bempedoic acid (Class I), not fibrates.
Both label and guidelines put fenofibrate after the statin; the guidelines demand LDL at goal and a number.

exercises.scenario: A high-risk patient on a statin has LDL at goal and triglycerides of 2.8 mmol/L.

questions.prompt: What do the 2019 ESC guidelines say about fenofibrate?
questions.explanation: Above 2.3 mmol/L with LDL at goal: IIb.

questions.prompt: Which option ranks higher for the same patient?
options: Gemfibrozil, which has the strongest outcome data (IIa)
questions.explanation: Icosapent ethyl is one step above the fibrates.

exercises.scenario: Label vs guideline on statin intolerance.

questions.prompt: Where's the sharpest contrast?
options: Statin replacement: label yes, guideline prefers others
They agree fully on every point
The guideline contraindicates fenofibrate alongside statins
The label forbids replacing a statin
questions.explanation: Guidelines don't change licences, but they shape practice.

questions.prompt: A 2021 EAS statement suggests fenofibrate in type 2 diabetes. How should it rank?
questions.explanation: Order of trust: SmPC, then guidelines, then consensus statements.

summary.title: The medicine and its story
points: A prodrug fibrate acting through PPARα: strong on triglycerides and HDL, modest on outcomes.
Formulation drives exposure: 145, 160 and 200 mg can be equivalent doses.
The 2009–2011 referral moved fibrates to second-line on benefit grounds.
Fenofibrate alone kept the statin add-on in the EU; the US removed fenofibric acid's in 2016.

exercises.scenario: A partner in Latin America asks why the EU still allows fenofibrate on top of a statin when the US doesn't.

questions.prompt: What's the best answer?
options: The two regulators read ACCORD differently
The EU had access to a newer trial
The EU product is a different molecule
questions.explanation: Same evidence, different regulatory readings.

questions.prompt: Which fact explains why lipid numbers look better than outcome data?
options: The outcome trials used the wrong dose
Markers and outcomes always move together
Lipids are markers; the outcome trials missed
The lipid figures came from different patients than the outcomes
questions.explanation: The module's most useful habit: marker ≠ outcome.

exercises.scenario: Link mechanism, formulation and history.

questions.prompt: Why could Fournier keep extending fenofibrate's life after 1975?
options: It gained new indications each decade
questions.explanation: Much of its later life was about formulation.

questions.prompt: Why isn't fenofibrate first-line for ordinary high cholesterol?
options: It's unsafe as a first treatment
It doesn't lower LDL at all, only triglycerides
Limited outcome benefit; statins come first
questions.explanation: Exceptions: statin intolerance and severe hypertriglyceridaemia.

questions.prompt: What does PPARα activation do to lipoprotein lipase and apo C-III?
questions.explanation: More stripping, less braking.

summary.title: The label in practice
points: Three lipid-defined uses, always with diet; no promise on events.
Products: interchangeable Secalip forms; combinations with simvastatin, pravastatin and rosuvastatin.
Dosing: with a meal; eGFR rules (below 30 no, 30–59 a dose this tablet can't give).
Monitoring: transaminases and creatinine early and periodically.

exercises.scenario: A 66-year-old, statin-intolerant, with mixed hyperlipidaemia, eGFR 72, soy allergy.

questions.prompt: Can she take Secalip Supra?
options: Yes: use 2 fits, and soy lecithin isn't an issue
Yes, at half the usual dose
No: the soy allergy rules it out
questions.explanation: Check contraindications after matching the indication.

questions.prompt: If she had no allergy, which indication applies?
questions.explanation: Fenofibrate stands in for the statin.

questions.prompt: What monitoring would follow?
options: Liver and kidney tests early on
Monthly CK tests for the first year
questions.explanation: Then both periodically.

exercises.scenario: A Spanish distributor wants to swap Cholib for separate tablets to save cost.

questions.prompt: Which label difference matters most?
options: Separate tablets are barred in diabetes
questions.explanation: One tablet versus two changes the rules, not just the packaging.

questions.prompt: Which combination requires the patient to already take both medicines at the same doses?
questions.explanation: Substitution only.

questions.prompt: Can a 160 mg tablet patient at eGFR 40 just split the tablet?
options: No: it must be swallowed whole
Yes, if the halves are taken with food
questions.explanation: The tablet can't meet its own label's dose limit.

summary.title: The evidence
points: FIELD and ACCORD-Lipid both missed their primary endpoints; secondary and subgroup signals only.
Drop-in, subgroups and interaction tests explain why the picture is uncertain, not negative.
Combination trials are short lipid studies; no outcome trial with ezetimibe.
No reduction in death or stroke; class benefit on coronary events is modest and relative.

exercises.scenario: An investor asks for a one-line verdict on fenofibrate's outcome evidence.

questions.prompt: Which is most accurate?
options: It has never been tested in an outcome trial
Primary outcomes missed; no effect on death
questions.explanation: Uncertain, not negative.

questions.prompt: Why might FIELD have underestimated the effect?
options: It was stopped early, before the effect could appear
It used too high a dose
Drop-in statins in the placebo group
It was too large to detect effects
questions.explanation: Drop-in narrows the gap between arms.

questions.prompt: Which subgroup result does the EU label print alongside the favourable one?
questions.explanation: Both are questions, not answers.

exercises.scenario: A partner proposes a triple combination (statin + ezetimibe + fenofibrate) for EU filing.

questions.prompt: What's the evidence base?
options: ACCORD-Lipid, which used simvastatin plus ezetimibe
questions.explanation: Effects on most lipoprotein fractions weren't additive.

questions.prompt: Which outcome has never been shown for fenofibrate?
options: Fewer total CV events in FIELD's secondary outcome
questions.explanation: Neither trial nor the pooled analysis showed a stroke benefit.

questions.prompt: A 13% relative reduction in coronary events across fibrates. What else do you need before using it?
options: A check of the US label
questions.explanation: Relative class effects don't give the size for a patient.

summary.title: Safety and guidelines
points: Safety centres on pancreas, clots, gallbladder, muscle (worse with statins), liver and creatinine.
Key interactions: anticoagulants (cut by a third), ciclosporin, glitazones, statins.
PSUSAs: maintenance; the women signal lives on in Cholib's RMP.
Guidelines rank fenofibrate low (IIb), behind icosapent ethyl, and not for statin intolerance.

exercises.scenario: A 72-year-old on simvastatin and warfarin is being considered for fenofibrate add-on.

questions.prompt: What has to happen with warfarin?
options: Stop it until the fenofibrate dose is stable
Cut it by a third; adjust by INR
questions.explanation: Fenofibrate strengthens oral anticoagulants.

questions.prompt: Why is extra muscle caution needed?
options: Simvastatin raises fenofibrate levels through CYP3A4
Over 70 plus a statin both raise the muscle risk
questions.explanation: Co-prescription is reserved for severe dyslipidaemia with high risk, no muscle history, strict monitoring.

questions.prompt: What do the guidelines say for him if LDL is at goal and TG is 2.5 mmol/L?
questions.explanation: LDL first, then optional next steps.

exercises.scenario: Trace how an uncertainty becomes a managed risk.

questions.prompt: Where did the 'more CV events in women' concern go after ACCORD-Lipid?
options: Into a direct healthcare professional communication
Into the SmPC, then Cholib's RMP
questions.explanation: It stays visible, labelled as uncertain.

questions.prompt: Which guideline change in 2025 affects fenofibrate's statin-replacement use?
options: Class I for ezetimibe and bempedoic acid
A new Class I recommendation for fibrates in intolerance
questions.explanation: Guidelines don't change the licence, but practice moves.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why did a referral with no new safety findings still restrict fenofibrate?
questions.modelAnswer: Benefit-risk is a balance. The referral found limited evidence of cardiovascular benefit, and better alternatives existed, so the benefit side shrank and first-line use was no longer justified.

summary.title: Fenofibrate: the whole picture
points: A prodrug fibrate: strong lipid effects, modest and uncertain outcome evidence.
Second-line since 2010–11, with a statin add-on kept in the EU only.
Formulations change exposure; kidney rules can make the 160 mg tablet unusable.
